title: Personal services income — Div 85 ITAA 1997
summary: Facet map: do the PSI rules apply? Spine: is it PSI (s 84-5 — mainly a reward for personal exertion) → employee/office holder/religious practitioner exception (s 85-35) → PSB gateway (any of the four s 86-15 tests or a determination — exit via s 85-30) → Div 86 attribution for entity-derived PSI (ss 86-20/86-25/86-30) → employee-equivalence deduction limits (s 85-10 with the s 85-10(2) preserved categories). FACETS: results test 75% threshold (s 86-15(2)), unrelated clients 2+ test (s 86-15(3)), employment test (s 86-15(4)), business premises test (s 86-15(5)), 80% rule / s 86-60 entity deductions, associate super SG cap (s 85-25(3)). Subsection coverage: ss 84-5, 85-5, 85-10(1)-(2), 85-15, 85-20(1)-(3), 85-25(1)-(4), 85-30, 85-35(1)-(2), 86-15(1)-(5), 86-20, 86-25, 86-30, 86-60 mapped; ss 86-75/86-80 determinations noted. Key ruling: TR 2022/3.

nodes.label: You earn income for personal work — do the PSI rules (Div 85/86) apply and limit your deductions?
nodes.body: Single question with facets. Spine: is it PSI → are you a PSB (exit) → entity attribution → employee-equivalence deduction limits. Facets carry the niche thresholds and where-to-look.

nodes.label: Is the income personal services income (s 84-5)?
nodes.body: PSI = income mainly a reward for your personal efforts or skills (the 'more than 50%' test). If the income rewards capital, equipment or others' work, Div 85/86 do not apply.

nodes.label: Not PSI — normal rules apply
nodes.body: If income is not mainly for personal exertion, it is business income under ordinary rules (s 6-5).

nodes.label: Are you an employee, office holder or religious practitioner (s 85-35)?
nodes.body: Div 85 does not apply to PSI received as an employee (s 85-35(1)(a)), office holder (s 85-35(1)(b) via Sch 1 TAA 1953 s 12-45(1)(a)-(e)), or religious practitioner (s 85-35(2) via s 12-47).

statute.title: Exception: employees, office holders and religious practitioners

nodes.label: Employee — normal employment deduction rules
nodes.body: Outside Div 85. Ordinary s 8-1 rules apply as an employee (TR 2020/1).

nodes.label: Do you conduct a personal services business (Div 86)?
nodes.body: If you pass any one of the four s 86-15 tests — results, unrelated clients, employment, business premises — or obtain a PSB determination (ss 86-75/86-80), you are a PSB and Div 85 does not apply at all (s 85-30). TR 2022/3 is the key ruling.

rulings.title: personal services income and personal services businesses

nodes.label: PSB — Div 85/86 do not apply
nodes.body: Income is business income; normal deduction rules apply. s 85-30 exempts the amount from Div 85.

nodes.label: Not a PSB — Div 85 deduction limits apply
nodes.body: You have PSI and are not a PSB. Div 85 now limits deductions to employee-equivalent amounts (subject to the s 85-10(2) exceptions). If the PSI is earned through an entity, Div 86 attribution and the s 86-60 entity deduction rule also apply.

nodes.label: Is the PSI derived through a personal services entity (company/trust/partnership)?
nodes.body: Div 86 attribution: the entity's PSI is attributed to you (s 86-20) unless paid to you promptly as salary (s 86-20(2)). The entity withholds under s 86-30 and its deductions are limited by s 86-60/86-25.

statute.title: When personal services income is taken to be that of an individual
General rule for deduction entitlements of personal services entities

nodes.label: PSI derived directly by you (sole trader)
nodes.body: The Div 85 limits apply directly: s 85-10 (non-employee deductions), s 85-15 (residence occupancy), s 85-20 (associate payments), s 85-25 (associate super).

nodes.label: Entity's PSI attributed to you (Div 86)
nodes.body: The PSE's PSI is attributed to you under s 86-20 unless promptly paid as salary. The entity deducts only what it could have deducted as an individual (s 86-25, aligned with s 85-10) and must withhold (s 86-30).

statute.title: When personal services income is taken to be that of an individual

nodes.label: Is the expense one an employee could deduct (s 85-10)?
nodes.body: s 85-10(1): no deduction for amounts relating to PSI that you could not deduct if you were an employee. s 85-10(2) preserves: (a) gaining work (advertising, tendering, quoting), (b) income/earning-capacity insurance, (c) liability insurance, (d) engaging a non-associate, (e) engaging an associate for principal work, (f) your own super, (g) workers' comp obligations, (h) other prescribed amounts.

statute.title: Deductions for non-employees relating to personal services income

nodes.label: Deductible (employee-equivalent or s 85-10(2) preserved)
nodes.body: Expenses an employee could deduct (work tools, professional development) are deductible; s 85-10(2) categories preserved. TR 2020/1 illustrates the employee baseline.

nodes.label: Not deductible under Div 85
nodes.body: Denied: not employee-deductible (s 85-10(1)), residence occupancy (s 85-15), associate payment outside s 85-20(2), or associate super outside s 85-25(2). Payments to associates denied are not income of the associate either (s 85-20(3)).

nodes.label: FACET — Results test (s 86-15(2)): 75% threshold
nodes.body: Where to look: s 86-15(2); TR 2022/3. Pass if (a) at least 75% of the PSI is for producing a result, AND (b) you are required to supply plant/equipment/tools of trade (unless the work involves mainly intellectual effort AND the income is not PSI of another). The 75% is of the PSI received during the year. The ATO applies the test strictly — a retainer that pays for time rather than a result fails.

rulings.title: personal services income and personal services businesses

nodes.label: FACET — Unrelated clients test (s 86-15(3)): 2+ clients, no direction
nodes.body: Where to look: s 86-15(3); TR 2022/3. Pass if you obtained PSI from 2 or more entities that are not associates of each other or of you, AND the PSI was not produced as a result of you being told what to do and how. Marketing to the public is the practical evidence. A single dominant client (80%+ of income) usually fails this test.

rulings.title: personal services income and personal services businesses

nodes.label: FACET — Employment test (s 86-15(4))
nodes.body: Where to look: s 86-15(4); TR 2022/3. Pass if during the year you (or your PSE) engaged an entity to perform work that is not PSI of the engaging entity, AND at all times the work was performed by individuals who were not employees of the engaging entity and not paid PSI by it. Practical effect: you genuinely engage others to do the work.

rulings.title: personal services income and personal services businesses

nodes.label: FACET — Business premises test (s 86-15(5))
nodes.body: Where to look: s 86-15(5); TR 2022/3. Pass if you (or your PSE) maintain business premises (NOT your or an associate's residence) at which you mainly perform the work, the premises are used mainly to produce the PSI, and they are physically separate from the acquirer's premises. Premises used by a DIFFERENT PSE of yours do not count.

rulings.title: personal services income and personal services businesses

nodes.label: FACET — The 80% rule and entity PSI (s 86-60)
nodes.body: Where to look: s 86-60; TR 2022/3. s 86-60: a personal services entity cannot deduct an amount relating to an individual's PSI unless (a) the individual could have deducted it in the same circumstances (employee-equivalence), or (b) the entity receives the PSI in conducting a PSB. The related 80% concept: where an entity derives PSI and less than 80% comes from one source, the entity may itself be a PSB (see the PSB determination rules).

statute.title: General rule for deduction entitlements of personal services entities

nodes.label: FACET — Associate super cap (s 85-25(3)): SG ceiling
nodes.body: Where to look: s 85-25. You can deduct super for an associate whose work forms part of the principal work (s 85-25(2)) — but the deduction is capped at the super guarantee amount you would have had to contribute for the associate (s 85-25(3)-(4)). The cap is calculated on the salary/wages not denied by ss 85-10/85-20.

edges.label: No — not mainly for personal exertion
Yes — passes a PSB test / determination
No — fails all four tests, no determination
